title: HostPort injection causing pod evictions and scheduling cascade - incident notes
body:
Summary:

At ~2025-11-03T03:22UTC we observed a sharp uptick in pod evictions and Unscheduled pods across cluster-prod-us-west-2. Root cause traced to a rolling deploy of the sidecar injector that started injecting a default hostPort (15001/tcp) into a high-replica backend deployment. The hostPort injection caused frequent port collisions on nodes (hostPort already bound), which surfaced as PodCreate failures and then accelerated into MassEviction behaviour as kubelet and kube-scheduler attempted to reconcile conflicting port reservations.

Impact:
- ~120 pods failed to start over a 20-minute window across 8 nodes (evictions and PodCreate failures).
- Several backend pods on healthy nodes were evicted as kubelet attempted to enforce port allocation constraints, causing request errors (5xx) for a small percentage of traffic (~3% of p95 latency spikes).
- Cluster autoscaler did not immediately add capacity because hostPort predicate still blocked scheduling on newly created nodes until kube-proxy/kubelet reconciled, which extended degradation.

Detection / Alerts triggered:
- Prometheus alert: KubeletPodCreateErrors > 50 / 5m (fired at 03:24 UTC)
- EvictionRate anomaly on SRE dashboard (03:25 UTC)
- Pager oncall at 03:26 UTC (Diego Morales)

Initial Triage timeline (UTC):
- 03:22 - Deployment rollout began for sidecar-injector: image v2.14.0. New webhook started returning mutated pods with hostPort: 15001 by default.
- 03:23 - First pod create error observed: PodCreate failed on node ip-10-0-12-45 (error: hostPort 15001 already allocated).
- 03:24 - Prometheus alert for pod create errors. Oncall starts triage: run 'kubectl describe pod' on failing pods.
- 03:26 - Several nodes show repeated events: "Failed to allocate port 15001: already in use" in kubelet logs.
- 03:28 - Eviction storm: kubelet starts evicting pods that hold ephemeral resources; scheduling backlog increases.
- 03:33 - Autoscaler attempts to add nodes but new nodes still show port conflicts for the webhook-injected hostPort until kube-proxy / kubelet startup completes.
- 03:36 - Quick mitigation: rollback sidecar-injector to v2.13.7 and pause rollout; restart kubelet on 3 most impacted nodes; flush conntrack on nodes with lingering TIME_WAIT sockets.
- 03:48 - Error rate subsides and PodCreate errors drop to baseline.

Root Cause Analysis (why this happened):
- A regression in sidecar injector (PR #142) changed default annotation behavior so hostPort: 15001 was injected for health-check/proxy sidecar. Test coverage missed this because our unit tests assert annotation presence, not content.
- Many backend services run with multiple replicas per node (high consolidation). With hostPort set on each pod, scheduling constraints become node-unique (only one pod per node could bind 15001). This sharply reduced effective bin-packing and exposed a latent assumption in the deployment manifest that sidecars would not use hostPorts.
- Kubelet reports show "port already allocated" event when new pods attempted to schedule. Some nodes also had orphaned socket holders: crashlooping containers left kernel sockets in TIME_WAIT or processes that regained the port on restart (systemd cgroup races). This caused transient failures even after rollback until processes and conntrack entries were cleaned.

Why autoscaler didn't immediately fix it:
- Cluster autoscaler increases node count but predicate evaluation still checks hostPort allocation; newly created nodes with kube-proxy/kubelet start-up timing created a window where port allocation logic returned conflicts until kube-proxy rewrote iptables rules and kubelet reconciled local port allocations. The autoscaler therefore could not quickly absorb the unmet schedule demand.

Detection details (commands we ran):
- kubectl describe pod <failing-pod>
- kubectl get events --field-selector involvedObject.kind=Pod -n backend --sort-by=.metadata.creationTimestamp
- journalctl -u kubelet -n 200 | grep "port .* already allocated"
- ss -ltnp | grep 15001 || true
- lsof -i tcp:15001 || true
- sudo conntrack -L | grep 15001 || true
- iptables -t nat -L -n | grep 15001 || true

Immediate mitigations performed:
- Rolled back injector to v2.13.7 (stopped injecting hostPort). This removed new mutations.
- Cordoned most-impacted nodes briefly (3 nodes) to avoid additional scheduling churn while we cleaned state.
- On cordoned nodes: restarted kubelet (systemctl restart kubelet) to get kubelet to re-evaluate port allocations.
- Flushed conntrack entries related to 15001 (sudo conntrack -F -p tcp --dport 15001) when safe to do so.
- Restarted kube-proxy on a subset of nodes to ensure iptables rules were consistent after rollback.
- Monitored PodCreate errors and eviction metrics until stable (~03:48 UTC).

Post-incident analysis and contributing factors:
- Mutating webhook / sidecar injection lacks a strict integration test for hostPort and node-level predicates. Unit tests cover 'inject' but not interaction with scheduler constraints.
- Some teams rely on hostPort semantics for legacy services, so the mutation change had broader blast radius than the injector owner expected. Lack of inter-team coordination (no opt-out sandbox enforced) contributed.
- Kernel-level TIME_WAIT and lingering sockets can make port refuse to be re-bound quickly after a crash; we didn't have automation to quickly identify and clear those for affected ports.

Action items (owners and ETA):
- Prevent accidental hostPort injection in CI: add a gate in k8s-sidecar-injector repo to fail builds that add hostPort by default (owner: Lin Zhao, ETA: 2025-11-10).
- Add integration test in staging that deploys a high-density workload and validates no hostPort mutation occurs (owner: Maya Thompson, ETA: 2025-11-12).
- Update mutating webhook to allow per-namespace opt-out and explicit opt-in annotation for hostPort usage (owner: Sidecar team, ETA: 2025-11-17).
- Create runbook entry for hostPort collision incidents with exact triage commands and safe conntrack/iptables procedures (owner: Aisha Patel, ETA: 2025-11-07).
- Dashboard: Add Prometheus panel and alert for 'kubelet_pod_start_failure_reason{reason="HostPortConflict"}' (owner: Diego Morales, ETA: 2025-11-09).
- Autoscaler: add an integration test or tuning to verify that a scaled up node progresses from NotReady->Schedulable in expected time window and to surface hostPort predicate failures separately (owner: Platform Eng, ETA: 2025-12-01).

Runbook / Playbook additions (draft):
- If alerted for PodCreate failures with reason HostPort conflict:
  1) Identify the failing pods and which node they attempted to land on (kubectl describe pod).
  2) Check kubelet logs on the target node for "port already allocated" events.
  3) Check host process bindings: ss -ltnp | grep <port>. If a process is bound unexpectedly, note PID and cgroup; determine if it belongs to a running container.
  4) If orphan kernel sockets are present (TIME_WAIT, CLOSE_WAIT) and no process is bound, coordinate a controlled restart of kubelet / kube-proxy on that node after cordoning it.
  5) If a mutated webhook caused the hostPort injection, roll back the webhook config in the control plane (pause rollout) and remove the injection annotation from deployment manifests if necessary.
  6) If conntrack entries are the issue, flush specific entries: sudo conntrack -D -p tcp --dport <port> (do not run -F unless cluster owner approves; we limited to specific entries during incident).

Monitoring / metrics to add:
- KubeletPodCreateErrors by reason (HostPortConflict, ImagePullBackOff, etc).
- Eviction rate per node + churn metric when > X per minute.
- Metric for webhook mutation rate with histograms of mutated fields (track when hostPort appears).
- Alert when a single port (e.g., 15001) is in use on > 70% of nodes unexpectedly.

Notes-to-self / open questions:
- Should we hard-fail webhook changes that add node-scoped features (hostPort, hostNetwork, hostPath) without an explicit multi-team approval?
- How to better simulate high-density scheduling in CI to catch these constraints? Can we create a synthetic high-consolidation test cluster?
- Consider a small admission controller hack: if injector tries to add hostPort and the namespace is in 'platform-managed' list, reject automatically.

Postmortem status: Draft. Waiting on sidecar team to sign off on the code-change gate (Lin / Sidecar owners). Full postmortem will be published to Confluence after validation of tests and runbook additions (target publish date: 2025-11-14).

Appendix (raw snippets captured during triage):
- Example kubelet event:
  "Failed to allocate port 15001: port is already allocated to container 3f8b2a"

- Safe conntrack delete used: sudo conntrack -D -p tcp --dport 15001 && sudo systemctl restart kubelet

- Commands to check mutation: kubectl get pod -n backend -o yaml | grep hostPort -n || true

- Slack thread pointers: #sre-ops oncall 03:27 UTC (thread id: slack-msg-9872)
